title: 6. Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet

epigraph.quote: “Operating cash flow was negative at Rs 45.8 crore for H1 FY27”
epigraph.author: Yahoo Finance, H1 FY2027 results summary [17]

web_blocks.html: The forensic record uses the consolidated statements in the snapshot for six fiscal years, FY2021 to FY2026, and the September 2026 balance sheet. The trailing column appears in the profit table only and is not mixed with annual cash flows. Where the company’s standalone figures differ, the difference is labelled.

web_blocks.caption: AZAD: consolidated profit and loss, FY2021 to FY2026 and trailing (₹ crore)
web_blocks.takeaway: The trailing column is shown for reference and is not used with annual cash flows.

web_blocks.html: Profit before tax of ₹187 crore in FY2026 depended on ₹46 crore of other income. Without it, operating profit less interest and depreciation would be ₹141 crore. The trailing column shows what the build costs: sales are ₹684 crore, yet trailing profit before tax is ₹179 crore, below the FY2026 figure, because depreciation has risen to ₹72 crore and interest to ₹41 crore while other income fell to ₹32 crore. Operating margin improved; the profit that reaches shareholders did not improve in step.

Interest needs its own note. It was ₹52 crore in FY2023, the year profit before tax fell to ₹13 crore, and it has risen again since FY2025. Profit before tax less net profit implies a tax charge of about 25% to 38% of pre-tax profit across the record, and the snapshot’s tax line reads 27% to 36%. Either way, tax has not been the source of the swings in profit. The swings come from operating profit, financing cost and other income.

web_blocks.caption: AZAD: consolidated balance sheet, March 2021 to September 2026 (₹ crore)
web_blocks.takeaway: Equity is mostly reserves. Borrowings rose faster than net worth from March 2025 to September 2026.

web_blocks.html: The balance sheet shows an equity base that is mostly reserves: ₹1,381 crore at March 2025, ₹1,516 crore at March 2026 and ₹1,583 crore at September 2026, against equity capital of ₹13 crore. Borrowings rose from ₹263 crore to ₹474 crore and then ₹578 crore. Net worth (equity capital plus reserves) was ₹1,394 crore, ₹1,529 crore and ₹1,596 crore on the same dates, so borrowings were 0.19, 0.31 and 0.36 times net worth.

The ₹700 crore QIP is not visible in that equity line. Reserves rose by about ₹67 crore between March and September 2026, close to the first-half profit of ₹67.2 crore [16], and equity capital did not move. The release describes ₹621.8 crore deployed and ₹78.2 crore retained [19]. Either the issue closed after the balance-sheet date or the snapshot does not carry it. The sources read do not settle the timing, so this pass does not count the proceeds as equity.

web_blocks.caption: AZAD: consolidated cash flow, FY2021 to FY2026 (₹ crore)
web_blocks.takeaway: Operating cash flow is negative in three of six years; the build is financed by outside money.

web_blocks.html: Cumulatively, operating cash flow for FY2021 to FY2026 was negative ₹56 crore, against net profit of ₹329 crore. Investing outflows totalled ₹1,294 crore and financing inflows ₹1,368 crore, so the capacity and working-capital build was met by outside money and new capital. The snapshot’s free-cash-flow row, negative ₹691 crore in FY2026, uses a capex definition that does not match the investing line of negative ₹71 crore, and this pass does not rely on it.

The cash-to-operating-profit ratio tells the same story. Dividing operating cash flow by operating profit, both from the tables above, gives 18% in FY2021, 34% in FY2022, negative 14% in FY2023, negative 6% in FY2024, 34% in FY2025 and negative 53% in FY2026. The snapshot’s own CFO/EBITDA row reads 43%, 41%, negative 1%, 7%, 44% and negative 31%, on a definition the table rows do not reproduce, so this dossier uses the computed figures. Three years were negative and the other three ranged from 18% to 34%. Cash has never converted fully, and the worst year is the most recent one.

web_blocks.caption: AZAD: working-capital days and returns, FY2021 to FY2026
web_blocks.takeaway: Debtor days reached their highest level in FY2026 while return on capital employed stayed at 12%.

web_blocks.html: Debtor days were 156 in FY2021 and 189 in FY2026, the highest in the series; working-capital days rose from negative 11 to 304. Return on capital employed was 22% in FY2022 and 12% in both FY2025 and FY2026, which means the new capacity has not yet earned the return the earlier base did.

Four basis differences need to be stated plainly. First, FY2026 operating cash flow is negative ₹119 crore on the consolidated basis and negative ₹123.3 crore on the standalone basis [23]. Second, borrowings at March 2026 are ₹474 crore consolidated and ₹451.6 crore standalone [27]. Third, debtor days for FY2025 are 178 in the consolidated snapshot, while the Exencial analysis gives 158 for FY2025 and 142 for FY2024 [32]. Fourth, FY2026 revenue is ₹603 crore consolidated, but the call basis is about ₹590 crore, and the segment shares are built on that call basis [8]. Each difference is in the sources. The blind pass uses consolidated figures for the statements and labels standalone figures where they appear.

Quarterly figures check the half-year. The consolidated quarters give sales of ₹173 crore in June 2026 and ₹191 crore in September 2026, a half of ₹364 crore, close to the ₹3,635.34 million (₹363.5 crore) reported [22]. Net profit for the two quarters is ₹66 crore in the snapshot, against ₹67.2 crore in the release [16]. The gap of about ₹1 crore is a basis difference, not an error this pass can resolve.

The bull reading of the forensic record is specific. Net profit rose from ₹12 crore to ₹134 crore over five years. Operating margin is 37%, and trailing margin is 38%. Borrowings are 0.31 times net worth at FY2026, a moderate level. Half-year revenue growth is still near 29%, and the working-capital build is partly a function of growth that the company is delivering.

The bear reading is equally specific. Operating cash flow was negative in three of six years and negative across the cumulative period. Trailing profit before tax is below FY2026 despite higher sales. Working capital is absorbing profit, borrowings are rising faster than net worth, and other income has been a large share of pre-tax profit. Each reading rests on the figures above, and neither is resolved by the sources read.

What would change this read is a run of positive operating cash flow alongside falling working-capital days, and an equity line in the next balance sheet that reflects the QIP. This pass stops at the business and the balance sheet, and the forensic verdict rests on the cash record.
